title: [Bug]: zai/ models lose max_output_tokens (or every call fails with drop_params=False)

labels.name: priority:medium
labels.description: For bugs, a serious source of annoyance, but not blocking a large number of users.

body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### Bug Description

For `zai/*` models the SDK sends the output limit as `max_completion_tokens`, but LiteLLM's zai provider only accepts `max_tokens`. With the default `drop_params=True` LiteLLM silently drops it, so `max_output_tokens` has no effect for these models. With `drop_params=False` every call fails.

### Expected Behavior

The limit reaches Z.ai as `max_tokens` and the call works, same as with other providers.

### Actual Behavior

- `drop_params=True` (default): the request body has neither `max_tokens` nor `max_completion_tokens`.
- `drop_params=False`: `LLMBadRequestError: litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: zai does not support parameters: ['max_completion_tokens'], for model=glm-5.3`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an `LLM` with `model="zai/glm-5.3"`, `max_output_tokens=1234` and `drop_params=False` (code below, runs offline with no key).
2. Call `llm.completion(...)`.
3. It fails with `UnsupportedParamsError` before any request is sent.
4. With the default `drop_params=True` and `base_url` pointed at a local mock server, the call succeeds but the request body has no output limit at all. `openai/glm-4.6` against the same mock sends `max_completion_tokens: 1234`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For `zai/*` models, the output limit is sent as `max_tokens`
- [ ] Providers that accept `max_completion_tokens` are unchanged
- [ ] A test checks the actual request body, not just the kwargs

### Installation Method

From source: git clone + uv sync

### If you selected "Other", please specify

_No response_

### SDK Version

1.63.1 (main @ 15bbd077d)

### Version Confirmation

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the LATEST version of OpenHands SDK

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Model Name (if applicable)

zai/glm-5.3 (also zai/glm-4.6)

### Operating System

_No response_

### Logs and Error Messages

```
openhands.sdk.llm.exceptions.types.LLMBadRequestError: litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: zai does not support parameters: ['max_completion_tokens'], for model=glm-5.3. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy:

`litellm_settings:
 drop_params: true`
```

### Minimal Code Sample

```python
from openhands.sdk import LLM
from openhands.sdk.llm import Message, TextContent

llm = LLM(model="zai/glm-5.3", api_key="test", base_url="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1",
          max_output_tokens=1234, drop_params=False, num_retries=0, usage_id="repro")
llm.completion([
    Message(role="system", content=[TextContent(text="You are helpful.")]),
    Message(role="user", content=[TextContent(text="hi")]),
])
```

### Evidence and Additional Context

Looks like the cause is `select_chat_options` in `openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/options/chat_options.py`, which only renames `max_completion_tokens` to `max_tokens` for Azure. `litellm.get_supported_openai_params(model="glm-5.3", custom_llm_provider="zai")` includes `max_tokens` but not `max_completion_tokens`.

LiteLLM 1.108.3.

I'd like to fix this. My idea is to send `max_tokens` whenever LiteLLM says the provider supports it but not `max_completion_tokens`, instead of adding another provider special case.

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Verified on `main` (v1.64.0): `select_chat_options` in `openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/options/chat_options.py` injects the output limit as `max_completion_tokens` and only renames it to `max_tokens` for `azure/*`, while LiteLLM's zai provider (repo-pinned 1.108.3, confirmed in its source) lists `max_tokens` but not `max_completion_tokens` in `get_supported_openai_params`. With the SDK default `drop_params=True` (forwarded to LiteLLM) the param is silently dropped, so `max_output_tokens` has no effect on `zai/*` models; with `drop_params=False` every call fails with `UnsupportedParamsError` before any request is sent. The reporter's offline reproducer and root-cause analysis are complete, and the proposed capability-driven rename matches repository guidance (root AGENTS.md: LLM behavior tweaks belong in `model_features.py` when expressible as model/provider capabilities; prefer solutions that make special cases disappear). Existing precedent is the Azure special case in `select_chat_options` and the `_normalized_supported_openai_params()` discovery helper.

Bounded scope: on the chat-completions path, send the injected default output-limit param as `max_tokens` for providers whose LiteLLM supported-params include `max_tokens` but not `max_completion_tokens` (zai is the verified case). Prioritized `priority:medium`: real user report with a reproduced failure in the actual SDK (confirmed on the latest version), but limited to one provider family with a silent-misconfiguration default and a hard failure only under `drop_params=False`.

Non-goals:
- No change to the Responses API path (`select_responses_options` keeps sending `max_output_tokens`).
- No new hardcoded `zai` provider special case in `llm.py` or `chat_options.py`.
- No change to user-supplied kwargs precedence: callers explicitly passing `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` keep today's behavior (including Azure's existing rename of user-supplied values).
- No change to extended-thinking (`max_tokens` + `budget_tokens`) or the Azure rename behavior.
- No change to the public `LLM` config surface (fields, defaults, serialization).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For a `zai/*` model with `max_output_tokens` set (default `drop_params=True`), the chat-completion request body handed through LiteLLM contains `max_tokens` with that value and does not contain `max_completion_tokens` — verified by a test that captures the actual request at the transport boundary (patched `litellm.completion` capture as in `tests/sdk/llm/test_llm_completion.py`, or a local mock `base_url` asserting the JSON body), not just the intermediate kwargs.
- [ ] With `drop_params=False`, `llm.completion()` for a `zai/*` model no longer raises `UnsupportedParamsError`; the issue's offline repro proceeds past parameter validation.
- [ ] Providers that accept `max_completion_tokens` are unchanged: `tests/sdk/llm/test_llm.py::test_advertised_output_limit_is_not_a_request_default` and `tests/sdk/llm/test_chat_options.py::test_azure_renames_max_completion_tokens_to_max_tokens` pass without modification.
- [ ] The rename is capability-driven via the existing provider-features discovery in `openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/utils/model_features.py` (per root AGENTS.md guidance), with no new per-provider string check for zai in `llm.py` or `chat_options.py`.
- [ ] The public `LLM` config surface is unchanged (no added/renamed/removed fields, defaults, or serialized settings), and the persisted-settings compatibility checks pass.
